symptom.actual: The production PM Rust contract required a Python test harness while Factory and Bench skipped that harness and reported cargo check as test evidence. The first native-test correction then executed untrusted Rust tests directly in the target workspace, accepted cargo exit-zero with zero discovered tests, and mislabeled rustc fallback evidence.
symptom.expected: Rust contracts declare native tests; every physical quality projection executes cargo test in an isolated disposable workspace, requires at least one discovered native test, and reports compile-only fallback evidence accurately without mutating target artifacts.

mechanisms: An internal Bench Python verifier convention leaked into the production PM Rust contract.
Factory and Bench validation gates executed generated Rust test binaries with the target workspace as writable cwd, bypassing Director mutation authority.
Cargo exit status was treated as sufficient evidence even when libtest reported zero tests.
Generic rustc metadata compilation was reported as cargo test and wrote .rmeta output into the target workspace.
Rust TASK-3 lacked read-only context_files required to author tests against the crate's public API.
root_cause.architectural_violation: Bench may consume platform evidence but may not define production project semantics. Factory/Bench quality gates are measurement authorities, not target-project mutation authorities.

final_request_and_runtime_evidence.authority_exploit: A generated tests/product.rs overwrote src/lib.rs while Factory returned passed=true before sandboxing.
final_request_and_runtime_evidence.zero_test_false_green: A Cargo crate with no native tests returned exit 0 and was previously reported as cargo test passed.
final_request_and_runtime_evidence.rustc_evidence_drift: A non-Cargo Rust file was reported as cargo test passed and left libmain.rmeta in the workspace.

fix_contract.producer: Rust PM synthesis declares tests/product.rs, cargo test, and read-only model/engine context_files while keeping write targets limited to tests/product.rs and README.md.
consumers: Factory workspace quality executes cargo test --quiet in a bubblewrap-isolated disposable workspace copy.
Internal real-run gate consumes the same isolated native validation primitive.
Both consumers require native_test_count >= 1 for cargo-test evidence.
Generic rustc fallback writes only to a temporary out-dir and is labeled rustc compile evidence.

forged_evidence_guards: reject project target linker/runner/rustflags/rustdocflags and test alias overrides
reject build and environment overrides that can replace or inject rustc, rustdoc, the linker, flags, loader, target, or executable path
reject harness=false custom lib/bin/example/test/bench targets across the root package and the recursive Cargo workspace closure, including explicit members and in-root path dependencies
ignore stderr for native test count

forbidden: target-project mutation by Factory or Bench gates
Python as a mandatory Rust project dependency
cargo check presented as executed test evidence
zero-test cargo success presented as test evidence

verification.red_evidence: Six initial focused regressions failed before the authority, zero-test, context, and rustc-evidence fixes. Nine additional adversarial cases failed before closing root Cargo target custom-harness and linker/rustflags paths. Two further cases failed before closing build.rustdoc and declared workspace-member paths. One final case failed before closing Cargo's implicit in-root path-dependency member closure.
verification.focused_green: 18 passed, including absolute original-workspace write denial, support-directory symlink escape denial, every Cargo target custom-harness class across root and recursive workspace manifests, compiler/rustdoc/linker/rustflags override forgery rejection, and sandbox-unavailable fail-closed cases.
verification.factory_characterization_scope: 11 Rust-selected passed after the second adversarial remediation; 23 passed before it

findings: Project-controlled .cargo-home symlink was followed during host-side support-directory preparation.
Native test count trusted forgeable stderr/custom-harness text.
independent_review_round_1.remediation: Support directories moved outside the copied project; dangerous Cargo execution hooks and harness=false are rejected; count requires paired standard-libtest stdout.

findings: Only [[test]] harness=false was rejected; [lib], [[bin]], [[example]], and [[bench]] custom harness targets could forge standard-libtest output.
Project Cargo target linker and rustflags overrides could replace the test executable and forge standard-libtest output.
Regression coverage omitted the corresponding Cargo target and execution-override classes.
independent_review_round_2.remediation: All Cargo target kinds now reject harness=false. Cargo build/target/env execution overrides that can replace the compiler, linker, flags, loader, target, or executable path now fail closed. Nine adversarial red-to-green cases cover the bypasses.

findings: Cargo build.rustdoc could replace the doctest executable and forge paired standard-libtest output.
Only the root Cargo.toml was audited, so a declared workspace member could retain a harness=false target and forge test output.
Regression coverage and the defect record omitted both bypass classes.
independent_review_round_3.remediation: build.rustdoc and its environment equivalent now fail closed. Declared workspace member manifests are resolved within the validation root and receive the same all-target custom-harness audit as the root manifest; unsafe or escaping member patterns fail closed. Two red-to-green cases preserve both bypasses.

findings: Cargo automatically adds in-root path dependencies to a workspace, but only explicit workspace.members were audited.
The workspace regression and defect record omitted the implicit path-dependency member closure.
independent_review_round_4.remediation: The workspace manifest resolver now computes a recursive closure over explicit members and Cargo dependency tables, including target/workspace/patch/replace path dependencies, rejects workspace escapes, and applies the same target-harness contract to every discovered member. A virtual-workspace red-to-green regression covers an explicit app whose implicit path dependency declares a custom binary harness.

workspace escapes, missing manifests, symlink manifests, and dependency cycles fail closed
root, explicit member, and implicit path-dependency member manifests share one target validator
